input: arr has n integers in[-1000000000,1000000000]. a,b,c are nonnegative safe integers. Require n*(n-1)*(n-2)/6<=9007199254740991 when n>=3. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. JavaScript integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: Number of index triples i<j<k satisfying abs(arr[i]-arr[j])<=a, abs(arr[j]-arr[k])<=b and abs(arr[i]-arr[k])<=c.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; only private working state is used. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Value differences have magnitude at most2000000000; all comparisons and absolute values are exact. Count is bounded by the number of triples, including all repeated-value/index combinations. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n^3+1) worst-case time/O(1) auxiliary space. Pair filtering can skip the innermost loop but does not change the worst-case bound. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 539 UTF-8 bytes, including every helper, Solution wrapper, signature, loop, built-in call, annotation/comment, whitespace and terminal newline.
